entities.summary:
Founded in 1996 by Park Jin-young, JYP Entertainment has emerged as a pivotal institution in the South Korean music industry, playing a crucial role in the global proliferation of K-pop. Headquartered in Cheongdam-dong, Seoul, JYP has shaped the careers of numerous influential artists, including Rain, Wonder Girls, GOT7, TWICE, and Stray Kids, thus making significant contributions to the cultural landscape both in East Asia and worldwide. With its innovative training system and marketing strategies, the company has not only expanded its influence within South Korea but has also established a robust presence in international markets, including North America and Europe.

The label's success is underpinned by its unique approach to artist development, which combines rigorous training in singing, dancing, and performance with strategic international promotions. Notably, in 2018, TWICE's album “Twicetagram” achieved remarkable sales, surpassing 1 million copies, illustrating the commercial viability of K-pop globally. JYP's concerts and global tours have attracted millions of fans, contributing to a cultural phenomenon that has drawn attention to South Korean music and entertainment as a whole.

As a result of JYP's efforts, the K-pop genre has transformed from a regional curiosity into a dominant force in the global music industry, inspiring countless artists and labels worldwide. The rise of K-pop has also led to increased cultural exchanges between South Korea and other countries, fostering a greater understanding of Korean culture and language. Today, JYP Entertainment stands as a model for other entertainment companies looking to replicate its success in the international arena.

In the words of Park Jin-young, 'We believe that music can break barriers and connect people.' This philosophy has not only guided JYP's operations but has also resonated with a diverse global audience, leading to K-pop's status as a transformative cultural movement in the 21st century.
